newsitem.title: MEXICO: ICA says Merida III gas duct bid not lowest.
newsitem.headline: ICA says Merida III gas duct bid not lowest.

text.p: Mexican builder Empresas ICA was notified by the government that its consortium's bid for the Merida III gas pipeline construction was not the most competitive, analysts said on Wednesday.
The pipeline will supply natural gas to fuel the planned Merida III power plant in the Yucatan peninsula, expected to require an investment of about $350 millon.

Company directors said in a conference call with analysts earlier this week that the price at which it offered to build the pipeline was not the lowest, but said it could still be in the running for the project's concession.

"They told us the government said their offer was not the lowest," Mexico City Serfin Securities analyst Gerardo Saenz said. But he added that ICA had not necessarily lost, because part of the result depended on the financing package.
Other analysts who participated in the conference call said ICA was unlikely to win the concession. ICA bid for the project with Epic Yucatan, Gas del Sur and Snam Spa.
The winning bidder is expected to be decided in the next week.

Other vyers for the concession are: Gasoductos Enron de Yucatan; Nova Corporation with The Williams Companies Inc. and Perez Companc International Ltd.; Gutsa Construcciones with Merida Pipeline Company Ltd and Transcanada Pipelines Ltd ; Bufete Industrial with Shell Oil Co and Mitsui Co Ltd.
